items.title: fix(websearch): block non-public URLs in page fetching
items.body:
## Summary

`WebSearchTool.fetch_page` accepted arbitrary model-supplied URLs and passed
them to Jina Reader, the direct urllib fallback, and the Playwright fallback
without restricting the destination. This allowed SSRF against loopback,
RFC1918, link-local, multicast, and cloud-metadata addresses (for example
169.254.169.254 and 100.100.100.200), and redirects were followed without
re-validation.

This adds `ms_agent/tools/url_safety.py`:

- accepts only `http`/`https` URLs with a hostname;
- resolves the hostname and rejects the request if any resolved address is
  loopback, private, link-local, multicast, reserved, unspecified, or
  otherwise non-global;
- unwraps IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses and strips IPv6 zone IDs;
- rejects known metadata hostnames and `.localhost` / `.local` / `.internal`
  suffixes;
- re-validates every redirect target in the urllib opener.

The check runs before Jina Reader, before the direct HTTP fallback, and on
every document navigation in the Playwright fallback, so a public URL cannot
redirect into an internal one. `ContentFetcher` now documents that local
fetchers must enforce this.

Fixes #1018

## Test

- `pytest tests/tools/test_url_safety.py tests/tools/test_server_tools_smoke.py -q` — 41 passed, 3 skipped
- `flake8` / `yapf 0.32` / `py_compile` on changed files — passed
- Reverting the Jina validation makes the regression test fail
- New tests cover private IPv4/IPv6 ranges, IPv4-mapped loopback, mixed
  public/private DNS answers, metadata addresses, redirects, and the
  Jina/Playwright entry points

## AI assistance

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); I reviewed the diff, ran the tests,
and can explain and defend the change.

items.title: feat(community): add Keenable web search provider

labels.name: area:backend
labels.description: Gateway / runtime / core backend under backend/

labels.name: area:ci
labels.description: GitHub Actions, CI config, repo tooling

items.body:
## Why

Keenable is a web search API for AI agents with its own index, and it has a keyless endpoint, so DeerFlow users can try it without signing up. This adds it as one more opt-in community `web_search` provider next to the existing ones. Disclosure: I work at Keenable.

## What changed

- New `deerflow.community.keenable.tools:web_search_tool`, opt-in via `config.yaml`. It is shaped like the You.com provider (#6515): same layout, key resolution, shared `coerce_max_results` owner, error JSON and test style.
- With no key it calls `POST https://api.keenable.ai/v1/search/public`. With `KEENABLE_API_KEY` (or `api_key` on the tool entry) it calls `POST https://api.keenable.ai/v1/search` with `X-API-Key`. Endpoint and headers are chosen together, so a key is never sent to the keyless endpoint.
- Every request sends `X-Keenable-Title: deer-flow` (the keyless endpoint returns 400 without an app name).
- Returns `[{title, url, snippet}]`, plus `published_at` when Keenable has it. Snippets are capped at 1500 characters, so a default 5-result search (about 8.5k chars) stays under the 12000-char `externalize_min_chars` default. `max_results` is capped at 50 because the API rejects larger values.
- Malformed HTTP-success payloads return the provider's format error, the same rule Sofya and Serply follow. Missing, null or empty `results` keep "No results found".
- Commented example in `config.example.yaml`, an entry in the `make setup` wizard (no key prompt, like You.com), doctor's free-provider list, `CONFIGURATION.md`, and a "Keenable" tab in the en/zh `harness/tools.mdx` docs.
- Registered in `test_search_max_results_single_owner.py` as a shared-owner provider.

It is opt-in and changes no default: DuckDuckGo stays the default `web_search`, no existing entry is reordered, and nothing calls Keenable unless an operator enables this tool. What goes to Keenable: the search query and `max_results`, the `X-Keenable-Title` header, and the API key if one is set. There is no fetch tool, so no page URLs are sent. httpx only, no new dependency, `uv.lock` unchanged.

## Surface area

- [ ] **Frontend UI**: page / component / setting / interaction under `frontend/`
- [ ] **Backend API**: endpoint / SSE event / request-response shape under `backend/app`
- [ ] **Agents / LangGraph**: agent node, graph wiring, `langgraph.json`, or prompt change
  - Prompt-layer self-check: for every data source in the new text, what is its trust level, and which channel should it ride? Model-supplied or user-influenceable values belong on the untrusted, sanitized data channel (e.g. the task `HumanMessage`), never interpolated into framework-owned system text, even neutralized.
- [ ] **Sandbox**: `docker/` or sandboxed execution
- [ ] **Skills**: change under `skills/`
- [ ] **Dependencies**: new/upgraded entry in `backend/pyproject.toml` or `frontend/package.json` (say what it buys us)
- [ ] **Default behavior change**: changes existing behavior without the user opting in (default model, default setting, data shape)
- [ ] **Docs / tests / CI only**: no runtime behavior change

None of the boxes fit exactly: this is a new opt-in community tool plus docs. The only `frontend/` change is docs content (`src/content/{en,zh}/harness/tools.mdx`).

## Screenshots / Recording

No UI change. The docs tab renders in the built `/en/docs/harness/tools` and `/zh/docs/harness/tools` pages.

## Validation

Backend:

- `cd backend && make lint`: ruff check passed, `ruff format --check` 2236 files formatted. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on `scripts/doctor.py` and `scripts/wizard/providers.py` also pass.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_keenable_tools.py`: 42 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_search_max_results_single_owner.py tests/test_youcom_tools.py tests/test_setup_wizard.py tests/test_config_version.py tests/test_keenable_tools.py`: 180 passed. `tests/test_doctor.py`: 153 passed.
- The full offline suite (same selection as `make test`: `-m "not live" --ignore=tests/blocking_io`, run locally in file chunks): 34,447 passed. One timing-sensitive test, `test_project_trash.py::TestStartupSweep::test_shutdown_hook_reports_a_late_finish_as_a_finish`, failed under load and passes on rerun. It does not touch this code.
- `make test-blocking-io`: 262 passed, 1 skipped.
- `python scripts/check_agent_guidance.py --base-ref upstream/main --head-ref HEAD`: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Frontend (docs content only):

- `pnpm format`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=local-dev-secret pnpm build`: all pass. `make test`: 3306 passed. E2E not run.

Live, keyless (`KEENABLE_API_KEY` unset), through DeerFlow's own loader: a config with the Keenable `web_search` entry, `get_available_tools(groups=["web"])`, then `web_search.invoke(...)`:

| query | max_results | results | non-empty snippets | output chars | latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LangGraph multi-agent orchestration | default (5) | 5 | 5/5 | 8761 | 344 ms |
| LangGraph multi-agent orchestration | 10 | 10 | 10/10 | 17538 | 489 ms |
| latest Python 3.13 release notes | default (5) | 5 | 5/5 | 8218 | 524 ms |
| latest Python 3.13 release notes | 10 | 10 | 10/10 | 15040 | 398 ms |
| how does retrieval augmented generation work | default (5) | 5 | 5/5 | 8616 | 508 ms |
| how does retrieval augmented generation work | 10 | 10 | 10/10 | 17172 | 399 ms |

The median latency was 444 ms. With a dummy key, the tool switches to `/v1/search` and returns `Keenable API error: HTTP 401 (invalid or expired KEENABLE_API_KEY)`. `scripts/doctor.py` reports `ok | Keenable (works with no key; KEENABLE_API_KEY lifts the keyless rate limit)` for that config.

## AI assistance

**Tool(s) used:** Claude Code

**How you used it:** Claude Code wrote the module, tests and docs from a spec, modeled on the You.com provider (#6515), and ran the checks above. I reviewed the diff.

- [ ] I've read and understand every line of this change and take responsibility for it. It's not unreviewed AI output.

items.title: perf: optimize browser architecture, preserve popup state, and validate on Oracle VPS
items.body:
## Architecture implementation and recovery complete; acceptance results below

Branch: `perf/browser-architecture-20260917`. Current pushed head: `886ea8eb8f832ce1bb0045615a18b9169e35685c`. Tested runtime: `29d21c9d95d1d8682ec9dc8ffe9aa9b03792e27b`. The final commit adds only documentation and explicitly inactive archived experiments; a full diff confirms runtime, tests, dependencies and workflows are identical to the tested runtime. Main remains at `1398bd0bd3c1c327ad9140d92f7351798807511e`. No force push or merge into main.

### Implemented architecture

- Run-owned event-driven popup handling instead of the unconditional popup delay or URL replay. Original POST/tab-local state and concurrent-run isolation are preserved.
- Explicit navigation readiness and Back/BFCache recovery; version-checked Browser Control 0.7.1 owned-popup compatibility patch.
- Bounded full/incremental/focused DOM membership collection with private stable refs, prioritized context and phase/payload metrics.
- Current document, target, semantic, focus, modal and associated-form checks. Sensitive values are redacted before truncation, with overlapping values matched longest first.
- Compact self-contained control state for Jev's independent questions, available-action filtering, direct field fill, unchanged-fill suppression and explicit-URL startup.
- At most two fresh observations after a proven pre-dispatch rejection, within twelve decisions. Unknown action outcomes never replay browser input.
- Autocomplete/select-only combobox support, active-modal scoping and bounded advisory readiness for declared popup editors.
- Writer output schemas and runtime boolean/string validation. Optional explanations remain optional. One typed inference timeout may retry the same model; cancellation is not retried. This never wraps a browser action.

### Completed on the requested Oracle VPS

All seven verification commands completed with exit 0 on `free` for the source published at this head:

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Vitest regression tests | **108 passed across 27 files** |
| Additional Node integration checks | **27 passed** |
| Typecheck and production build | **Passed** |
| Credential-free harness safety | **Six assertions passed** |
| Canonical real-extension browser journeys | **10/10 passed** |
| Additional real-extension deterministic journeys | **10/10 passed** |

Actual Chromium, Browser Control extension and relay were used for both browser suites. Small-fixture timings: **112 ms median focus click**, **101 ms redirect navigation**, **143 ms Back recovery**. These are not a paired before/after comparison or a universal website speedup.

### Final secret-backed acceptance

[Hosted Actions run 35287450407](https://github.com/victortran0904/Jev-Browser-Use/actions/runs/35287450407) tested runtime commit `29d21c9`; the final documentation-only head has identical executable source. GitHub injects `GEMINI_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` only into the live steps. This hosted run is distinct from the completed Oracle tests above. Final job outcomes are recorded here after completion, not inferred from fixtures.

| Final hosted gate | Actual outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Regression, typecheck, build and invariants | **Passed** |
| Deterministic browser journeys | **10/10 passed** |
| Live Jev/Gemini fixture journeys | **10/10 passed** |
| Public flight-search prompt | **Failed: low-confidence stop before input** |
| Selected result artifact uploads | **Passed** |

The ten live fixtures used **34 TypeSafe and five Gemini HTTP requests**, with no HTTP failures. The separate public attempt used **three TypeSafe and two Gemini requests, all HTTP 200**, but stopped after **6,360 ms** when the proposed Enter action scored **0.25**, below the unchanged **0.30** threshold. That Enter action was not sent to the browser. No qualifying real fare was verified; the overall workflow is therefore failed, not all green. Results are retained in Actions and locally under `evidence/final-completion/run-29d21c9-live/` and `run-29d21c9-public/`.

This is an agent/public-site acceptance failure, not a missing API key or current VPS-disconnection claim. No confidence, request-budget or fare-evidence assertion was relaxed to make the report pass.

Original public prompt remains exactly:

> find me a flight from hanoi to vancouver in  december for less than 2,500$

Acceptance assumptions are separately labeled: December 2026, CAD, one-way economy and one adult. No booking, account/payment entry or CAPTCHA bypass is permitted. A manual diagnostic or synthetic fixture is not an autonomous-agent fare-search pass.

Historical failures remain visible. The earlier `61e09bc` hosted checkpoint passed 10/10 live fixtures but its public attempt timed out. Run `35286464623` at `501cc43` passed deterministic checks but failed two writer-stage cases and a low-confidence fixture; its public test stopped at confidence 0.28. Subsequent tests reproduced an unnecessarily strict optional-explanation check and fixed it, then added native provider output schemas. Raw provider bodies were not logged, so that issue is not asserted to explain every historical failure.

### TDD and both review stages

The user waived subagents. Actual vertical RED/GREEN cycles and specification self-review followed by code-quality/safety self-review are documented under `docs/plans/architecture-optimization/`, especially `RECONNECTED-REVIEW.md` and `COMPLETION-REVIEW.md`. Both review stages were repeated for the writer compatibility/schema correction. No independent-agent, Copilot or Greptile approval is claimed.

### Recovery and cleanup

All previously unfinished implementation files, airport-option coverage, numeric public-flight diagnostics and review notes were reconciled and pushed. The two active worktrees now match this published head and are clean. The older experimental worktree is clean; its superseded collector is archived as non-production evidence rather than reintroduced. No source changes are left only in an uncommitted active worktree.

No temporary runner registration, runner directory or browser process remained in the final Oracle cleanup check. No new self-hosted runner was provisioned after the earlier provisioning restriction. Keys were not printed or extracted; browser/relay processes use an allowlisted environment. Reports contain selected status/count/timing metadata, not raw model bodies or browser profiles. Raw local test logs remain outside source control under `evidence/final-completion/`.

### Explicit limitations

Two optional follow-up experiments were not applied after tool safety checks blocked their implementation commands: a production per-attempt model deadline and changed-page-only recovery from a low-confidence decision. Their genuine RED tests are explicitly archived as `archive/deferred-writer-deadline.test.ts.txt` and `archive/deferred-uncertain-state-recovery.test.ts.txt`, not counted as active passing tests or implemented fixes. No alternate route was used to apply the blocked writes. Existing verification deadlines and confidence behavior remain; the shipped timeout retry bounds attempts, not total production duration.

The lightweight observer is not a complete cross-origin iframe/shadow accessibility engine. Sensitive-field and modal heuristics are not universal. Arbitrary compound submissions remain excluded. Public-fare evidence is conservative and currently requires route/date/CAD amount together in one text line; a real-site extraction improvement must preserve their association, not accept unrelated cheap prices.

For an existing installation, run `npm ci`, reload the bundled extension and restart the relay. The Browser Control 0.7.1 popup patch requires review on dependency upgrade. **This PR remains draft and unmerged pending final acceptance; no success is claimed for an unverified flight.**

items.title: feat(eve)!: what a person sends is eve's own MessageContent
items.body:
### Summary

Every send, `deliver` result and schedule took the AI SDK's `UserContent`. That tied eve's input contract to AI SDK types and hid eve's own file schemes in their fields. `MessageContent` is the subset eve already accepted: text and file parts, with a file's data inline or as a URL. Part literals pass unchanged; image parts go. The harness converts to AI SDK content where it builds model messages. **Breaking:** the input types change from `UserContent` to `MessageContent`. Stacked on #4602.

Release notes for this atomic 19-PR stack are centralized in #4726, including the final template changes. This PR has no separate changesets.

Workflow agent sessions also accept `MessageContent<string | URL>` instead of text alone. URL file parts survive local prompt formatting and remote dispatch; URLs serialize as strings. Inline bytes, base64, and data URLs fail before a durable send. Text-only prompts retain their existing wording. Failure reasons stay plain strings: `AgentMessageResult.error.message` is not message content. Related to #4930.

Production code: **98 more lines (+384/−286)**. Adds eve-owned text/file types and URL-only workflow message normalization; adapters convert at the model boundary instead of exposing peer-SDK input types. Excludes tests/fixtures, generated copies, docs, and tooling.

### Validation

- Four focused unit files passed all 59 tests in 1.83 seconds, using `vitest.unit.config.ts`: workflow message validation, delegated prompt formatting, remote agent transport, and agent-session dispatch.
- Combined-head package typecheck and declaration emission pass after restoring the scalar error-message type. Intermediate boundaries are not independently green claims.
- `pnpm docs:check`, formatting, lint on edited TypeScript, and `git diff --check` passed.
- No full integration or scenario tier run. Earlier full-stack validation predates this retcon.

Latest type-only follow-through at assembled head `390f9e5b3`: `AgentMessageResult.error.message`
is restored to `string`. Package typecheck/declaration build, targeted lint, formatting, and diff
checks pass. Runtime tests were not rerun for this annotation-only correction. The invariant guard
reports only the unreleased `tool/v93` contract hash; generation remains deferred to the agreed
final assembled-source pass. No reports or baselines were rewritten.

### Checklist

- [x] I added tests and documentation where relevant
- [x] I added a changeset if this touches the published `eve` package (atomic-stack release notes centralized in #4726)
- [x] DCO sign-off passes for every commit (`git commit --signoff`)

items.title: ops: separate public product contracts from live operations
items.body:
## Summary

- remove duplicated operator skills, hosted recovery recipes, exact live-provider inventory, production commands, verification queries, and secret matrices from public product surfaces
- preserve product architecture and configuration contracts, schema-dependent migration/backfill ownership, the isolated restore fixture, generic observability assets, and transitional Fly deployment definitions
- freeze the public Ory workflow at manual plan-only and constrain public identity restore to the protected development environment
- require restore targets to be resolved from direct Ory project URLs through the Ory JavaScript SDK workspace inventory and to match an independently stored expected project ID

## Validation

- `pnpm run check:actionlint`
- `node --test infra/ory/*.test.mjs` (5 passing)
- bounded live SDK resolution returned the expected development project ID without printing credentials or workspace inventory
- `pnpm exec nx test @themoltnet/node-red-contrib-core` (94 passing)
- `pnpm --dir docs build`
- all commits have valid Git signatures
- searches find no private operations repository reference or known exact live Ory, Fly, or Axiom identifiers

## Operational boundary

This PR changes public ownership boundaries and workflow safety only. It does not apply or restore Ory configuration, create billable resources, access Strongbox, or change production infrastructure. The bounded development lookup used the existing GitHub Environment credential only to resolve and verify the direct project URL. Live operations remain outside the public product repository.
